The handler accepts all HTTP verbs. Any GET/PUT/DELETE request that passes the webhook secret check will attempt to read and process req.body, which will be empty or undefined for GET requests, causing zod.parse to throw a 500 instead of a clean rejection. Add a method check before the auth check.

symmetricDecrypt can throw synchronous errors from the Node.js crypto module (e.g. wrong key length, bad ciphertext format), and JSON.parse throws on non-JSON strings. Neither is wrapped, so a malformed or tampered keys payload returns an unhandled 500 instead of a 4xx. Wrap both in a try/catch and return res.status(400).

When credential sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response from the self-hosted endpoint. A native Response object has no .data property, so res?.data is undefined and token.access_token immediately throws a TypeError. This is swallowed by the outer try/catch — returning stale myGoogleAuth without updating the credential. Token refresh is silently a no-op for Google Calendar whenever sync is active. The fix is to branch on the response type: when the sync path is taken, read the body via res.json() before extracting access_token and expiry_date.

When the sync endpoint response omits refresh_token (which is expected — self-hosted syncs typically only return a new access token), this fallback saves the literal string "refresh_token" to the credential. If credential sync is later disabled, any subsequent normal OAuth refresh will use this bogus value as the actual refresh token, causing an invalid_grant error and marking the credential invalid. Consider omitting the field or preserving the existing value rather than storing a placeholder.

Zod schema objects do not override toString(), so both computed keys in the object literal resolve to identical strings and the second overwrites the first. The resulting schema only enforces access_token (a string), never a numeric expiry field. The comment describing the intent is misleading. Using .passthrough() on a minimal base schema would be clearer and more correct.

Salesforce token refresh bypasses refreshOAuthTokens. All other adapters changed in this PR wrap their fetch calls in refreshOAuthTokens so the sync endpoint is invoked when credential sharing is enabled. The Salesforce getClient method calls the Salesforce token endpoint directly and is therefore excluded from the credential sync feature, even though parseRefreshTokenResponse was added.
